title: Grace-period coordinator for SLO relaxation and sticky fallback windows
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: During the recent regional incident (INC-2026-02-20) we observed repeated circuit toggles where short-lived healthy signals caused immediate reopen followed by rapid re-shedding. This led to request oscillation and a poor client experience. This PR introduces a centralized GracePeriodCoordinator that provides a sticky fallback window after a circuit transitions from open->closed so traffic is gradually ramped back rather than immediately routed at full weight.

What this implements: single continuous design change implemented as: 1) a lightweight coordinator living in the routing control plane that tracks per-region/per-model 'grace windows' triggered on circuit transitions; 2) sticky fallback policy that keeps requests routed to the fallback variant (or local-preserved fallback route) for the configured window, with jittered decay to avoid synchronized reopen storms; 3) a bounded soft-unwind mode used by the autoscaler to slowly increase route weight; 4) telemetry and debug endpoints for operators to inspect active windows and their provenance. The coordinator is policy-driven: customers and SREs can configure window length, decay curve, and max concurrent sticky windows to control capacity impact.

Why different from previous work: this is not a pure load-shedder or a circuit-state-only change — it introduces an explicit time-boxed 'sticky' period after a circuit closes to prevent oscillation. We intentionally decouple the coordinator from the core runtime so it can be toggled in Dedicated and Private without changing inference kernels.

Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1248) - [x] unit tests for coordinator state transitions and jitter behavior - [x] e2e smoke test for routing continuity with a local canary - [x] metrics (grace_window_created, grace_window_expired, sticky_routed_requests) - [x] runtime flag and config knob for window length - [x] docs updated (routing policies)

Commits summary: - feat(grace-coordinator): add coordinator service, state machine and store integration - feat(router): add sticky-fallback routing hook and policy evaluation - perf: cache active-window lookups in routing hot path with an LRU TTL - test: add unit/e2e tests and CI scenarios - fix: ensure coordinator persists window across small control-plane restarts

Files changed (high level): - internal/routing/coordinator.go (core coordinator + state machine) - internal/routing/policy.go (policy evaluation hooks) - internal/routing/middleware.go (routing hook and LRU cache integration) - api/routing/v1.proto (new RPC for debug listing and manual override) - docs/routing/grace_windows.md (operator guide + examples) - tests/e2e/grace_window_canary_test.go - charts/redwood/templates/router-config.yaml (toggle flag) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new metrics)

Testing and CI: CI initially reported a flaky e2e on kube-env (timeout) which I addressed by tightening backoff in the e2e harness and marking the test to use the canary namespace. After two reruns the CI status is green. Relevant checks: unit (pass), lint (pass), e2e (pass), integration (pass), security-scan (pass).

Review conversation (summary): - Riley Chen: requested stronger guarantees that windows will not be recreated on quick restart; author implemented persisted checkpoint and updated tests. - Sana Kapoor: asked for observability hooks; added metrics and /debug/grace-windows endpoint. - Liam O'Rourke: suggested decay jitter range be randomized per-region to avoid alignment; implemented region-level seed. Comments and replies are in the thread below.

Merge details: Squash-and-merge after approvals and redwood-ci green. No migration downtime expected. The change is behind a runtime feature flag (router.grace_windows.enabled=false by default) for staged rollouts.
